evidence.excerpt: Radovan Janković received his Dipl.Ing. in Industrial Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad in 1998, followed by an M.Sc. in 2002 and a Ph.D. in 2007, both from the same institution. His doctoral thesis addressed heuristic and exact methods for irregular polygon nesting in textile and leather cutting. He was appointed Full Professor in 2018. His research group focuses on computational geometry methods for 2D irregular nesting, marker-making optimisation, cutting-plan scheduling, and operations research techniques for minimising material waste in batch manufacturing. He teaches courses in operations research, production planning, and combinatorial optimisation. The group uses custom C++ and Python solvers, No-Fit Polygon libraries, and interfaces with commercial CAD/CAM cutting systems available in the faculty's Manufacturing Systems Laboratory.
